issues.legal_issue: A sale deed executed alongside an agreement to reconvey constitutes an outright sale rather than a nominal sale securing a loan when the deed and surrounding circumstances show an intention to transfer ownership absolutely.
material_facts: The property owner had borrowed money and had earlier mortgaged the property to the lenders.
On the same day, the owner executed a sale deed and an agreement to reconvey the property.
The sale deed recited an absolute transfer for consideration, stated that the owner and his heirs retained no right or interest, and provided for enjoyment and disposal by the purchasers.
The owner had already delivered possession and handed over property-related certificates, and the evidence did not contradict the sale deed’s terms.
The execution of the agreement to reconvey was established.
issues.conclusion: The sale deed was an outright sale, not a nominal deed or security for the loan; the established agreement to reconvey did not make the sale deed nominal.
issues.legal_principle: The true character of a transaction is determined from the document’s terms considered with the surrounding circumstances. Under Section 58(c) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, where the sale and the agreement concerning reconveyance are embodied in separate documents executed on the same day, the transaction cannot be treated as a mortgage by conditional sale. The Court relied on no earlier cases for this issue.

rule.if: specific_performance_dispute and same_day_sale_and_reconveyance_documents and sale_deed_has_absolute_transfer_terms and surrounding_evidence_supports_absolute_transfer

predicates.specific_performance_dispute: The claimant sought enforcement of an agreement concerning reconveyance of property.
predicates.same_day_sale_and_reconveyance_documents: The parties executed a sale deed and a related agreement to reconvey the property on the same day.
predicates.sale_deed_has_absolute_transfer_terms: The sale deed described an absolute transfer of ownership and denied the transferor any continuing right or interest.
predicates.surrounding_evidence_supports_absolute_t: The surrounding circumstances and evidence supported the sale deed’s description of an absolute transfer.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks enforcement of reconveyance and the same-day documents and surrounding evidence show an absolute transfer, the sale deed is treated as an outright sale rather than nominal security.

issues.legal_issue: Pleadings that sufficiently allege readiness and willingness satisfy the pleading requirement for a claim seeking specific performance.
material_facts: The claimant sought specific performance of an agreement to reconvey property.
The trial court found sufficient pleading concerning readiness and willingness.
The Supreme Court agreed that the pleadings sufficiently addressed readiness and willingness, while separately considering whether the claimant proved it.
issues.conclusion: The pleadings sufficiently complied with the requirement concerning readiness and willingness.
issues.legal_principle: Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 requires a claimant seeking specific performance to plead and prove readiness and willingness. The Court treated the pleading requirement as sufficiently met, without treating that pleading alone as proof of readiness and willingness.

predicates.specific_performance_claim: The claimant sought a decree requiring performance of an agreement.
predicates.plaint_alleges_readiness_and_willingness: The claimant alleged in the pleadings that he was ready and willing to perform his contractual obligations.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks specific performance and alleges readiness and willingness in the pleadings, the pleading requirement is satisfied.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant seeking specific performance must prove continuous readiness and willingness, including the means to arrange the required consideration, and a bare assertion of willingness is insufficient.
material_facts: The claimant alleged that he was ready to pay the consideration, but pleaded that he had no business, profession, source of income, or movable or immovable property.
Apart from a witness’s statement, there was no evidence that the claimant had the means to arrange the consideration.
Before filing suit, the claimant had sought relief to extinguish the debt and recover the property rather than to pay under the reconveyance agreement.
The reconveyance agreement provided for interest, but the claimant alleged that no interest was payable.
The property had been mortgaged to a bank, and the defendants paid the claimant’s debt after the bank obtained an award and the property was put up for auction.
issues.conclusion: The claimant failed to prove continuous readiness and willingness to perform his obligations, so specific performance was unavailable. The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s decree was set aside, and the trial court’s dismissal of the suit was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963, continuous readiness and willingness is a condition precedent to specific performance; a claimant must both aver and prove it. The court considers the claimant’s conduct before and after suit and all attending circumstances, and the required consideration must be shown to be available, though it need not be held as cash in hand if the claimant proves the means to generate it. The Court relied on N.P. Thirugnanam (Dead) by LRs. v. Dr. R. Jagan Mohan Rao and Others; Pushparani S. Sundaram and Others v. Pauline Manomani James (deceased) and Others; Manjunath Anandappa URF Shivappa Hanasi v. Tammanasa and Others; Pukhraj D. Jain and Others v. G. Gopalakrishna; and Umabai and Anr. v. Nilkanth Dhondiba Chavan (Dead) by LRs. and Anr.

rule.if: specific_performance_claim and (no_evidence_of_means_to_arrange_consideration or (sought_debt_extinguishment_instead_of_contractual_payment and denied_contractual_interest and defendants_paid_claimant_bank_debt))

predicates.specific_performance_claim: The claimant sought a decree requiring performance of an agreement.
predicates.no_evidence_of_means_to_arrange_consider: The claimant offered no evidence, beyond a witness’s statement, that he had the means to arrange the required consideration.
predicates.sought_debt_extinguishment_instead_of_co: The claimant sought an order extinguishing the debt and returning the property rather than establishing that he would pay under the reconveyance agreement.
predicates.denied_contractual_interest: The claimant disputed that he was required to pay interest even though the agreement provided for it.
predicates.defendants_paid_claimant_bank_debt: The defendants paid the claimant’s bank debt after the property faced auction.

issues.definition: When a claimant seeks specific performance and has no evidence of means to arrange the consideration or shows conduct inconsistent with the agreed payment obligations, specific performance is denied for failure to prove readiness and willingness.
